question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(\mu, 5^2)$ with $P(X > 2) = 0.2981,$ find $\mu.$

$z$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$$\, 0.03 \,$
$\, 0.5 \,$ $\, 0.695 \,$ $\, 0.6985 \,$ $\, 0.7019 \,$
$\, 0.6 \,$ $\, 0.7291 \,$ $\, 0.7324 \,$ $\, 0.7357 \,$
$\, 0.7 \,$ $\, 0.7611 \,$ $\, 0.7642 \,$ $\, 0.7673 \,$
question.explanation:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 2) &= 1 - P(X > 2) \\[3pt] &= 1 - 0.2981 \\[3pt] &= 0.7019 \end{align*} \]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 2) &= 0.7019 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{2-\mu}{5} \right) &= 0.7019 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{2-\mu}{5} \right) &= 0.7019 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2-\mu}{5} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.7019) \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(0.53) = 0.7019 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.7019) = 0.53. \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{2-\mu}{5} &= 0.53 \\[5pt] 2-\mu &= 2.65 \\[5pt] \mu &= -0.65. \end{align*} \]

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq -1.1) &= 1 - P(X > -1.1) \\[3pt] &= 1 - 0.2578 \\[3pt] &= 0.7422 \end{align*} \]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq -1.1) &= 0.7422 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{-1.1+3.7}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.7422 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{2.6}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.7422 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2.6}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.7422) \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X| \lt 3.2) = 0.7330,$ find $\sigma^2,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

$z$ $\, 0.01 \,$ $\, 0.02 \,$ $\, 0.03 \,$
$\, 1.0 \,$ $\, 0.8438 \,$ $\, 0.8461 \,$ $\, 0.8485 \,$
$\, 1.1 \,$ $\, 0.8665 \,$ $\, 0.8686 \,$ $\, 0.8708 \,$
$\, 1.2 \,$ $\, 0.8869 \,$ $\, 0.8888 \,$ $\, 0.8907 \,$
question.explanation:
First, we express the given probability as \[ P ( |X| \lt 3.2) = P(-3.2 < X < 3.2) . \]

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

\[\begin{align*} P(-3.2 < X < 3.2) &= 0.7330 \\[5pt] 2 P(0 < X < 3.2) &= 0.7330 \\[5pt] P(0 < X < 3.2) &= 0.3665\\[5pt] P(X < 3.2) - P(X < 0) &= 0.3665 \\[5pt] P(X < 3.2) - 0.5 &= 0.3665 \\[5pt] P(X < 3.2) &= 0.8665 \\[5pt] P(X \leq 3.2) &= 0.8665 \end{align*}\]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-coring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 3.2) &= 0.8665 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{3.2-0}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8665 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{3.2}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8665 \\[5pt] \dfrac{3.2}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.8665 ) \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(1.11) = 0.8665 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.8665) = 1.11. \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{3.2}{\sigma} &= 1.11 \\[5pt] \sigma &= \dfrac{3.2}{1.11} \\[5pt] \sigma &\approx 2.882\,88. \end{align*} \]

Finally,

\[\begin{align*} \sigma^2 &= (2.882\,88)^2 \\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{8.31} \end{align*}\]

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
